data.title: OpenAI cuts API, credit pricing of GPT-5.6 Sol
data.description:
• OpenAI (OPENAI) said on Friday that it has cut pricing for its Application Programming Interface and credit of its latest frontier model, GPT-5.6 Sol, by 20% for the next three months.
  • The ChatGPT maker made the announcement on its X account.
  • GPT-5.6 Sol was released in limited preview in late June before rolling out on a broader basis last month.

data.title: Eaton initiated Outperform at Baird as 'just getting started' capturing AI demand
data.description:
Eaton (ETN) up 1.4% in Friday's trading as Baird initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and $500 price target, saying the power management company is "just getting started capturing AI demand," as cloud still represents most data center sales currently, but orders were 50% AI in 2025.

Baird analyst Luke Junk said Eaton (ETN) is well-equipped for the upcoming transition to800VDC, recent M&A has created a broad AI infrastructure platform, and the point of maximum operating pain amid once-in-a-generation capacity expansion has passed.

Eaton (ETN) is now on the downslope of a once-in-a-generation expansion across 24 ElectricalAmericas sites, with Q1-Q2 marking the largest production ramp in management's model and 18 sites now online, and the added capacity helped unlock exceptional ~220% Electrical Americas data center order growth, while 2026 also marks peak M&A digestion, supported by new and dedicated global data center leadership, the analyst wrote.

Rising aircraft production is a down payment on future aftermarket business, where higher content on key platforms, anticipated 25% revenue passenger-mile growth through 2030, and strong one-in-two commercial air penetration overall support durable growth in revenue and margin, while the aerospace business adds a growing $1B market opportunity, Junk said.

data.title: Tesla leads China’s record vehicle recall over door safety
data.description:
China has begun its largest vehicle recall, with Tesla (TSLA) and 10 other manufacturers addressing safety concerns involving emergency access to vehicle doors.

The campaign covers almost 4.3 million vehicles, highlighting the growing regulatory focus on electronic systems as automakers race to add new technology to cars. Tesla (TSLA) accounts for the biggest portion, with about 2.98 million Model 3, Model Y, Model S, and Model X vehicles affected.

The recall centers on the possibility that occupants or rescuers may struggle to find or use mechanical door releases after a serious crash, particularly if a vehicle’s electrical system stops working. Tesla (TSLA) plans to add identification labels and distribute a software update that can lower the windows following a collision.

Other affected manufacturers include Xiaomi (XIACF), Leapmotor (ZJLMF), Xpeng (XPEV), and Geely (GELYF). Xiaomi (XIACF) will cover about 390,000 vehicles, while Leapmotor (ZJLMF) and Xpeng (XPEV) are recalling roughly 371,000 and 264,000.

The measures come as Chinese authorities increase safety oversight of the world’s biggest auto market. Beijing has also announced plans to prohibit concealed door handles from 2027, a feature increasingly common in electric vehicles.

Most of the fixes will be carried out remotely, limiting the need for owners to visit service centers and reducing the expense associated with traditional recalls.

data.title: Alibaba-backed robot company seeks $3B value in new funding - Bloomberg
data.description:
Chinese robotics startup Dexmal is looking for a valuation of around 20 billion yen ($3B) in an ongoing funding round.

The talks are continuing and come after a previous round that included Chinese AI lab Z.AI Co., also known as Zhipu,  according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited an interview with  Dexmal founder Tang Wenbin at the World Robot Conference in Beijing. The fundraising follows rounds led by Alibaba (BABA) and NIO Capital late last year.

Chinese top humanoid robot maker Unitree surged more than fivefold in its stock market debut in Shanghai on Wednesday. Unitree—known for its robots that perform dance routines, martial arts, and backflips—raised about $900M in its IPO.

Unitree is backed by Chinese tech giants including Tencent (TCEHY) and Alibaba (BABA) as well as state-owned enterprises. Its U.S. competitors include Tesla (TSLA)  and Hyundai (HJMLF)-owned Boston Dynamics.

data.title: Regulator sues ex-Bank of America investment banker over insider trading tip - report
data.description:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has sued ex-Bank of America (BAC) senior investment banker Jason Satsky over allegedly providing insider trading tip to a friend, Bloomberg News reported.

The alleged tip led to ~$18.5M in illegal profits, the report published on Friday noted.

data.title: If Treasuries were a 'safe haven' at $30T, what are they at $40T?
data.description:
Market strategists are raising pointed concerns about the traditional safe-haven status of U.S. Treasuries (IEF) (TLH) (TLT) (ZROZ) as the national debt crosses $40T, with some warning that a surge in corporate debt issuance from cash-strapped tech giants may be the primary force pushing yields higher.

"We always thought about treasuries, in particular short-term treasuries (SHY), as a safe haven," Eduardo Repetto, chief investment officer at Avantis Investors, said in a CNBC interview. "When you get to 40T, that's a big number. So maybe it's not as safe as we thought."

David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research, offered a structural explanation for why bond yields have climbed since February—and it has less to do with government fiscal policy than many assume. "It was just back in late February that the ten-year treasury note yield (US10Y) was trading below 4%," Rosenberg noted. "And it's not as if, since February, the fiscal policy has really changed."

The real culprit, according to Rosenberg, is the hyperscaler (AMZN) (META) (MSFT) (ORCL) (GOOG) (GOOGL) spending spree. "The really big issue that's happened in the past several months has not been about fiscal issuance. It's been about the surge in long-dated issuance by the hyperscalers," he explained. With three of the four major hyperscalers now running free cash flow negative, they've been forced to tap capital markets for funding—directly competing with the U.S. government for investor dollars at the long end of the yield curve.

This dynamic is compounding a concentration problem that Repetto says has been building for years in fixed-income portfolios. Because benchmark bond indexes are debt-weighted, the flood of Treasury issuance has dramatically shifted allocations without investors realizing it. "If you look at the Bloomberg, it has like 50% in government securities today. If you go twenty-five years ago, government securities were 20%," Repetto explained. "So suddenly, you are buying today an index Bloomberg Ag kind of ETF, it's more and more and more allocation to treasuries without even you knowing that you're changing your allocation."

Avantis has responded by taking a more active approach, deliberately reducing Treasury exposure. "We take a more active approach and say, how much treasury we really want versus corporate versus other securities," Repetto said. "You have to consider the treasury as one more participant in the market, and we have to decide how much to allocate versus what we get from that."

As for Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's recent bond buyback operation, Rosenberg believes the $4B initial move was merely a trial balloon. "I think that Bessent right now is just testing the waters," he said, noting that there's $4T of marketable debt outstanding with ten years or more maturity. "I get a sense that if he has to, he'll take out a big bazooka, not unlike what Ben Bernanke did."

The stakes are clear: "The government has drawn a line in the sand that it's not gonna allow the ten-year to get to 5%," he added.

data.title: Parsons upgraded at Baird as growth seen accelerating in this year's H2
data.description:
Parsons (PSN) up 5.5% as Baird upgraded the provider of design, engineering, and technical services to Outperform from Neutral with a $57 price target, raised from $48, saying "sentiment is low and guidance looks conservatively set," as H2 acceleration rests on the ramp-up of seasonal mine projects, $400M of OTAs that contributed nothing in H1, and a ~$40M JCHK ramp—"not new book-and-burn wins."

Baird analyst Andrew Wittmann said Parsons (PSN) management still expects the protested $190M award to clear and contribute lightly, and FAA scope could approach ~$800M—far better than December's fears, with agency growth tracking to 40% plus—and YTD BTB trends have "meaningfully improved" after an earlier soft patch.

Wittmann sees Parsons (PSN) as a leading player in higher-end professional and technical services for federal government and infrastructure customers which have strong secular demand growth profiles, having built a consistent reputation in the marketplace during its 78-year history; more recently, the company has built out an increasingly differentiated high-end talent base in the intel, cyber, and electronic warfare domains to complement its historical roles in missile defense and traditional federal services.

data.title: O-I Glass surges as Citi upgrades to Buy after YTD plunge
data.description:
O-I Glass (OI) up 10.4% in Friday's trading as Citi upgraded the manufacturer of glass containers to Buy from Neutral with a $9 price target, raised from $8, with a 90-day catalyst watch, saying the shares look meaningfully oversold after falling 57% YTD.

O-I Glass (OI) has been hit with higher energy costs from the Middle East conflict, operational issues leading to lower Fit-to-Win cost savings and higher costs, and a weaker European market on both demand and price, and Citi analyst Anthony Pettinari said after a series of negative revisions, he expects estimates have largely bottomed, and the low-end of FY 2026 EBITDA guidance could be reiterated on the Q3 earnings call in late October given conservative assumptions for an H2 volume recovery, stabilizing net pricing in Europe, and resolved operational headwinds.

The company updated FY 2026 EBITDA guidance to reflect operational issues leading to lower Fit-to-Win savings and higher costs, but Pettinari said he does not expect any carryover into H2 2026 or H1 2027, noting O-I (OI) closed three European plants in H1, stressing operating rates at other facilities while costs were rising after the start of the Middle East conflict; further, there was a furnace fire in France and a furnace leak in the U.K., and it was forced to pivot someshipping from rail to truck following unexpected disruption in France.

O-I (OI) said it now expects a $75M-$125M drag on EBITDA from lower net price, greater than the $35M-$100M assumed in April, due to heightened competitive pressure in an oversuppliedEuropean glass market, but the analyst expects performance could improve as the company benefits from a lower cost position and increased focus on high-value customers as Fit-to-Win initiatives accelerate in Europe.
